subsystems.name: Sail membrane
subsystems.role: the reflective surface that intercepts sunlight and turns it into thrust — kilometres of area for useful cargo masses, but only grams per square metre.
parts: polyimide film a few micrometres thick
aluminium reflective coating tens of nanometres thick
ripstops, seams and reinforced corner attach points

subsystems.name: Deployment structure
subsystems.role: holds the membrane flat and taut without a rigid frame heavier than the sail itself.
parts: thin-walled composite booms, flattened and rolled on spools

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the cargo and keeps the vehicle alive.

subsystems.name: Thrust-vector control
subsystems.role: tilts the sail so the thrust points where the trajectory needs it.
parts: electrochromic or liquid-crystal reflectivity-control panels on the membrane
moving trim masses or gimballed booms
small chemical or electric thrusters for the final approach

subsystems.name: Cargo and docking interface
subsystems.role: the payload canister and the means to hand it over.

buildSteps.title: Fix the trajectory first
buildSteps.detail: Because thrust depends on sail area and orientation, the spiral or transfer is designed before any hardware: how big the sail must be, how many months the trip takes, and how much the last few hundred metres per second cost in propellant.

buildSteps.title: Cast and coat the film
buildSteps.detail: Polyimide is cast to a few micrometres thick, then aluminised on one face to make it reflective and to control how it sheds charge.

buildSteps.title: Cut and seam the gores
buildSteps.detail: The film is cut into panels, joined with ripstops so that a micrometeorite hole stops at one seam, and reinforced wherever a boom or line attaches.

buildSteps.title: Make the booms
buildSteps.detail: Thin-walled composite tubes are cured in a flattened profile so they can be rolled onto a spool, then spring back to a stiff straight section on release.

buildSteps.title: Pack the sail
buildSteps.detail: The membrane is Z-folded around the stowed booms into a volume small enough for a launch fairing, with release ties that fire in sequence.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the bus
buildSteps.detail: Structure, solar cells, avionics, reflectivity-control panels and the cargo canister are integrated and shaken and thermally tested.

buildSteps.title: Deploy on orbit
buildSteps.detail: Release ties fire, booms unroll over minutes to hours, and the team checks that the membrane is flat and free of snags before trusting it with thrust.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the thrust
buildSteps.detail: Orbit tracking measures the tiny acceleration and how it changes with sail tilt — the data that turns the membrane into a navigable engine.

buildSteps.title: Fly the transfer
buildSteps.detail: Guidance trims the sail continuously for months, harvesting a fraction of a millimetre per second squared and summing it into kilometres per second — with no propellant consumed.

prerequisites.tech: Ultrathin deployable sail films and booms
prerequisites.why: sails of tens to a few hundred square metres have flown, including interplanetary demonstration missions; cargo-class sails are orders of magnitude larger.
the thrust is weaker than any perturbation, so the vehicle must compute and retrim its own path over months.

prerequisites.tech: Attitude control that steers thrust without using propellant
prerequisites.why: reflectivity-control panels and trim masses have been demonstrated, but only on small sails.
radiation darkens the film, micrometeorites perforate it and plasma charges it, slowly eroding thrust over a multi-year cargo run.
a sail cannot stop at a depot; something must close the final metres and latch the cargo.
a ground- or space-based laser could raise thrust by orders of magnitude and shrink the sail, but only concepts and small-scale experiments exist.

pathway.milestone: small sails (tens to about a hundred square metres) flying and trimming their orbits by photon pressure alone
pathway.unlocks: proof that the force is measurable, steerable and repeatable.

pathway.milestone: large sails of hundreds to a few thousand square metres on dedicated interplanetary small-satellite missions
pathway.unlocks: long-duration thrust data and realistic degradation rates.

pathway.milestone: a cargo demonstrator delivering a small payload to a cislunar or near-Earth-object depot
pathway.unlocks: the rendezvous, berthing and logistics chain around the sail itself.

pathway.milestone: routine propellant-free resupply of depots, with sails as the slow, cheap lane and chemical or electric tugs as the fast one
pathway.unlocks: a logistics architecture where launch mass goes to payload rather than to propellant.
